description: Stocks under the SEC Regulation SHO Rule 201 short sale restriction (SSR) for the current session, as the signal8.ai/short-sale-restriction-list page lists them. SSR is triggered when a stock falls 10% or more below its prior close during regular hours; while in effect, short sales are allowed only above the national best bid, for the rest of that day and the whole next trading day. `today` lists stocks triggered during sessionDate (restricted through the next session); `carriedOver` lists stocks triggered during previousDate (restricted all of sessionDate). On a weekend or holiday sessionDate is the next trading day and `today` is empty. Each row has ticker, name, exchange, triggerDate, triggerAt (ISO), movePct (move at the trigger vs the prior close, null = not measured), source and timeBasis. source "exchange_list" is the listing exchange's published Rule 201 list, with the exchange's trigger time: Nasdaq's list for Nasdaq-listed stocks, and NYSE Group's daily list for NYSE, NYSE American and NYSE Arca listings (published in the evening after the session, so a same-day trigger on those stocks is exchange_flag or computed until it lands, and the next-day carry-over is from the list; NYSE Group rows also carry deactivationDate, the exchange's first date the restriction no longer applies); source "exchange_flag" is the short sale restriction flag the NYSE and NYSE American trading status feeds publish for every listed stock they trade (exchange reported; triggerAt is the exchange's own timestamp, or null when the restriction was only seen restated before the next open); source "computed" is Signal8's own reading of stored prices, shown only when neither exchange source reported the stock and the flag feed did not cover that whole session, with timeBasis "minute_bars" (first regular-hours minute at the trigger, set the next morning) or "first_seen" (when a live price read first showed it; the real trigger can be earlier). A stock missing from the list is not confirmed unrestricted: computed rows are a lower bound. exchangeList (Nasdaq) and nyseList (NYSE Group) say whether each exchange's end-of-day list for each date has been read (final, partial, not_read); exchangeFlag says whether the flag feed covered each date's whole session (covered, not_covered). The optional ticker narrows both lists to one symbol. Preferred, right and warrant classes keep a lowercase class letter (AHTpD is AHT preferred D); the all-capitals form (AHTPD) also matches when no other security shares it.

ticker.description: Ticker to check (e.g. "AAPL", or "AHTpD" for a preferred class). Omit for the whole list.
